exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A smart-shopper report proves every deal with a unit rate — here is how one student compared art supplies.

traits.sample: The 12-pack of markers costs $6.00, or $0.50 each; the 8-pack costs $4.40, or $0.55 each — so the 12-pack wins.
traits.why: Both options become price-per-item, which makes the choice provable.

traits.sample: Choosing the big pack saved me $0.05 per marker, which is $0.60 across 12 markers.
traits.why: Savings are quantified per unit AND in total — not just called a better deal.

traits.trait: Uses percent to describe the discount
traits.sample: The sale price dropped from $5.00 to $4.00; that is a 20% discount because 1.00 ÷ 5.00 = 0.20.
traits.why: It converts the price change into a percent with the division shown.

traits.trait: Checks the total against the budget
traits.sample: My cart total of $23.75 is under my $25 budget, so my plan works with $1.25 to spare.
traits.why: Strong work always circles back to the real-world constraint.
